subject: Renewal health check — token mix, perf regressions, uplift rationale
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@crestline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health check — token mix, perf regressions, uplift rationale

Hi Asha,

Quick health check ahead of your Nov 1 renewal. We pulled a short snapshot of Q3 consumption and paired it with perf telemetry. High-level takeaways:

- Token mix: 72% embedding calls (short contexts), 28% generation (longer sequences). Generation tokens have increased average length by ~35% month-over-month.
- Cost drift: net per-token cost increased ~12% vs. Q2 due to the higher share of long generations and a small increase in model size (switched to v2.1 last month).
- Latency: two brief regressions on Sept 14 & Oct 3 linked to a model-serving config that increased KV-cache misses — see latency_regressions_q3.pdf.
- ROI signals: despite cost creep, feature-level metrics (answer relevance for customer-facing chat) improved ~7% after v2.1 — customers report fewer follow-ups.

Attachments: usage_snapshot_Q3.csv (token breakdown), latency_regressions_q3.pdf (timeline + stack traces), uplift_scenario_costs.xlsx (3 pricing/commit options).

Recommended path for renewal conversation:
1) Short-term: agree a modest uplift (+30% committed capacity) to smooth headroom during holiday traffic and capture current growth.
2) Mid-term: move generation-heavy flows to a model-quantized variant we validated (saves ~18%/token) — we'd schedule a rollout window with your infra team.
3) Governance: add a conditional cap that triggers an ops review if average latency >200ms for a 1h window.

Next actions I propose: 30-min call this week to walk the spreadsheet and align on procurement timing. Ben, can you run the uplift pricing scenarios for a 12-month commit with a 30% uplift vs. a 6-month bridge? Grace, can you confirm engineering runbook for the KV-cache patch?

Asha — what does your procurement timeline look like? Is Nov 1 a hard renewal or flexible by a couple weeks?

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

[Attachments: usage_snapshot_Q3.csv (csv), latency_regressions_q3.pdf (pdf), uplift_scenario_costs.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Asha Patel <asha@crestline.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@crestline.ai>, Procurement <procurement@crestline.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — token mix, perf regressions, uplift rationale

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we jump on a call:

1) For the 30% uplift, do you have an expected delta to monthly burn (ballpark $)? The spreadsheet is helpful but procurement wants a single-ballpark number to triage.
2) On the latency regressions: is the KV-cache patch already validated on a staging cluster? We cannot afford customer-facing latency spikes during our sales demo week (Oct 25–29).
3) Any downside to a 6-month bridge vs 12-month commit from your perspective?

We are aiming to have procurement approved by Nov 8, so Nov 1 is flexible by a week but we'd prefer to finalize before the middle of November.

– Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Product, Crestline AI
asha@crestline.ai | +1 212-555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — token mix, perf regressions, uplift rationale

Jonas — running numbers now. Preliminary figures (very ballpark):
- Current average monthly burn (Sept run-rate): ~$92k/mo.
- 30% uplift committed (12mo) scenario: effective blended price reduces ~15%, net monthly spend ~ $88k (after discounts & committed rate amortization) — spreadsheet has line-item math.
- 6mo bridge (30% uplift) yields less discounting; monthly spend ~ $96k but with greater flexibility.

Asha — the main tradeoff is predictable unit economics vs. flexibility. If you expect usage to keep growing >20%/mo we recommend 6 months bridge + scheduled review at month 4 with an opt-in for 12-month commit. If steady growth <=10%/mo then 12-month is financially preferable.

Grace — staging validation on KV-cache patch is in progress; engineering estimates a final smoke test by tomorrow EOD. If that passes we can offer a targeted 48-hour deployment window before your demo week.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@crestline.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health check — token mix, perf regressions, uplift rationale

Hi Asha — quick operational update:

- KV-cache patch: validated on staging (perf + correctness). We saw KV hit-rate improve by ~22% on production-like traces.
- Rollout plan: 1) small-canary in your us-west region for 2 hours (non-critical traffic), 2) ramp to 50% for 4 hours with monitoring, 3) full rollout. We commit to abort and rollback if tail latencies exceed +30% over baseline.
- Timing: we can schedule the canary on Tue 10/26 02:00–04:00 PT (off-peak for Crestline). That leaves the full rollout window the week after if everything looks green.

Jonas/Ben — given procurement target (Nov 8) my recommendation: sign a 6-month bridge with the 30% uplift and a committed review at month 4. That gives Crestline flexibility, buys headroom through holiday activity, and gives us the runway to complete the quantized-generation migration which will realize the token savings.

Asha — if that plan works for you I can attach an ops-runbook excerpt and a rollback checklist to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
